mediation

/mee-dee-AY-shun/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Mediation means the process in which a neutral third party helps two disputing sides talk through their conflict and reach their own agreement.

When the Nguyens and the Parkers could not agree on the property line, one afternoon of mediation at the community center settled the fence question for good.

Example

Instead of suspending both students, the school sent them to peer mediation, where a trained classmate helped them talk through the lunchroom conflict and write their own agreement.

The trained classmate is a neutral third party who doesn't take sides or hand down a punishment — she guides the two students toward an agreement they create themselves. That guided process is mediation.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

peacemaking: Peacemaking is any work that helps end a conflict, from a kind word to a treaty — the broad umbrella. Mediation is one specific, structured form of it: a neutral third party guides the two sides through talking until they build their own agreement.

intervention: An intervention is stepping into a situation to change its course, and the stepper-in often takes over or takes sides. Mediation is the opposite of taking over: the neutral guide holds no power and pushes no outcome — the disputing sides write their own agreement.

facilitation: Facilitation is guiding any discussion or process so it runs smoothly — a facilitator keeps a meeting on track whether or not anyone disagrees. Mediation exists only where there is a dispute: its whole point is helping two opposed sides reach their own settlement.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

instigation: deliberately stirring up a conflict

agitation: whipping up anger or unrest

Where it sits · how much power the third party holds — discussion → mediation → arbitration

discussion vs. mediation: A discussion is weaker than mediation — the two sides simply talk on their own, with no neutral guide keeping the conversation fair and on track.

arbitration vs. mediation: Arbitration is stronger than mediation — the third party doesn't just guide the conversation; an arbitrator hears both sides and hands down a binding decision they must accept.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — medi

Root — medi: middle (Latin medius)

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: the act or process of

Put it together

Put it together: Mediation is literally 'the process of standing in the middle.' A mediator plants themselves in the middle ground between two sides — belonging to neither — and helps them find their way toward each other.

Use the root in a new word: intermediate

Use the root in a new word: intermediate: After her third lesson, the ski school moved Lena up from the beginner class to the intermediate group.

Root Check

Word Choice

Formal — legal and civic register

Mediation is not the same as a court case: a judge or arbitrator imposes a decision, while a mediator only helps the two sides build their own agreement — often by encouraging each side to offer a concession or two along the way. Watch the spelling trap: mediation (settling a dispute) is one letter away from meditation (quiet focused reflection), and mixing them up changes the sentence completely.
